<description>
Part of #36692. Please view this PR in context of changes like https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36694.

`CTransaction` gains a constructor that allows direct declarative construction as an alternative to building through `CMutableTransaction`. `CTxIn`'s constructors gain an optional argument to pass the script witness.

It is a conscious decision that `vin/vout` are passed as generic input ranges and that only *their elements* are copied/moved.
Passing the `std::vector` by value and then moving the *container itself* into place would allow the following:

```cpp
std::vector<CTxIn> inputs = ...;
CTxIn& backdoor = inputs.back();

const CTransaction tx{std::move(inputs), ...};

backdoor = ...; // <- modify `tx`, potentially breaking its invariant
```
</description>

I added a few cases to show the new constructor in action. If the constructor would accept `std::vector` arguments, a transaction without inputs could be constructed as:

```cpp
auto tx = CTransaction{{}, {
    CTxOut{nValues[0], CScript{} << ToByteVector(key[0].GetPubKey()) << OP_CHECKSIG},
    CTxOut{nValues[1], CScript{} << ToByteVector(key[1].GetPubKey()) << OP_CHECKSIG},
}};
```

It is certainly less verbose, but I don't think it does a service to readability.
